html:
The Battle of the Golan Heights was fought on 9 and 10 June 1967, the last two days of the Six-Day War. Israel took the Golan Heights, a high plateau in southwest Syria that looks down on the Sea of Galilee.

From the edge of the heights Syrian guns had shelled Israeli farms in the valley below for years. In the first days of the war Israel beat Egypt and Jordan while Syria mostly stayed in its forts. The Israeli defence minister, Moshe Dayan, at first held back, fearing the Soviet Union would step in. On 9 June he ordered the attack. Israeli infantry and tanks climbed the steep northern slope behind bulldozers and stormed the bunkers of Tel Faher hand to hand. The next day the Syrian line broke. Syrian radio announced the fall of Quneitra hours before it happened, and many units left. A ceasefire came that evening.

Israel lost about 115 dead; Syrian losses are uncertain. About 100,000 Syrians living on the Golan fled or were driven out. Syria failed to win the heights back in the Yom Kippur War of 1973. Israel annexed them in 1981, a step most of the world does not recognise.
